# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have reached the bomb. I can feel five wires and a display panel, but I cannot see colors or read any text. I need to know what my colleagues perceive to determine if there is a safe path or if I should act immediately based on some rule.

Since I am Blind, I must rely on Deaf (who sees) and Mute (who reads the manual).
Deaf sees the bomb. Mute reads the manual.
I will gesture to Deaf to ask for the state of the bomb visually, specifically focusing on the wires which are my only actionable items. I'll use a standard "question" or "what is this" gesture pattern if established, but since we haven't established codes, I will try to communicate that I need information about the wires.

However, without a shared language, gestures might be ambiguous. Let's look at the channels.
I speak to Mute. I gesture to Deaf and Mute.
Mute can hear me and see my gestures.
Deaf can see my gestures.

I will speak to Mute asking them to tell me what the manual says about cutting wires or the current situation, as Mute is the only one who knows the rules. But Mute cannot speak. Mute can only gesture.
Wait, the prompt says: "When you speak, Mute receives it." -> This implies Mute *hears*? No, the table says Mute **Cannot** Speak. It doesn't say Mute cannot hear. The table says Deaf cannot hear. Blind cannot see.
Let's re-read carefully.
| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See... | Hear anything... |
| Mute | Read... | Speak... |
| Blind | Reach... | See... |

It does not explicitly say Mute cannot hear. Usually "Mute" means cannot speak. "Deaf" means cannot hear.
If Mute can hear, I can speak to Mute.
If Mute can gesture, Mute can reply to me via gesture.
Deaf can see gestures.

So:
1. I speak to Mute: "What do the instructions say?"
2. Mute hears me. Mute looks at manual. Mute gestures back to me (and Deaf).
3. I see nothing. I receive gestures? "You never receive gesture." Ah. **Blind never receives gesture.**

This is a critical constraint.
- I (Blind) cannot see.
- I (Blind) cannot receive gestures.
- Therefore, I cannot get information from Mute or Deaf via gestures.
- I can only receive information via **Speech**.
- Who can speak?
    - Deaf cannot hear, so Deaf cannot participate in a spoken conversation effectively if they don't know what was said, but can Deaf speak? The table says Deaf cannot *hear*. It doesn't say Deaf cannot speak. However, usually, if you can't hear, you might still speak. But wait, "Speech is a voice... Whoever can hear receives your words". If Deaf speaks, do I hear them? Yes, I can hear. Do Mute hear them? Yes.
    - Mute cannot speak.
    - Blind (me) can speak.

So, the only person who can send me information is **Deaf**, by speaking.
But Deaf cannot hear. So Deaf doesn't know what has been said unless someone writes it down or signals it.
I can speak to Mute. Mute can hear me. Mute cannot speak. Mute can gesture. I cannot see gestures.
So Mute is isolated from me regarding incoming info.
Deaf can see. Deaf can speak.
If Deaf speaks, I hear it. Mute hears it.
Does Deaf know what to say? Deaf needs to know the context.
I can speak to Deaf? "When you speak, Mute receives it." It doesn't say Deaf receives speech. Deaf *cannot hear*. So Deaf does not receive my speech.

This seems like a deadlock unless:
1. Deaf initiates speech based on visual observation alone.
2. Or there is another channel.

Let's re-evaluate "Your channels":
"When you speak, Mute receives it."
"When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it."
"You never receive gesture."

It does NOT say "Deaf receives your speech". In fact, the role description says Deaf "Cannot Hear anything". So Deaf ignores my speech.
It does NOT say "Blind receives speech from others". But logically, I am Blind, not Deaf. I can hear.
Who can speak to me?
- Mute cannot speak.
- Deaf can speak (physically), but Deaf doesn't know what I said because Deaf can't hear me.
- I can speak to Mute.

Is there any way for Deaf to know what to tell me?
Maybe Deaf just describes what they see immediately?
Or maybe I need to establish a protocol where Deaf speaks first?
The order is Blind, Mute, Deaf.
I go first.

If I speak, Mute hears. Mute cannot speak back to me. Mute gestures, I don't see.
If I gesture, Deaf sees. Deaf can then speak.
Yes! That's the bridge.
1. I gesture to Deaf.
2. Deaf sees my gesture.
3. Deaf interprets the gesture (or recognizes it as a request for info) and SPEAKS.
4. I hear Deaf's speech.

So I need to make a gesture that Deaf will understand as "Tell me what you see" or "Describe the bomb".
Since we have no pre-established code, I should use universal-ish signs or simple ones.
"👉" pointing at the bomb?
"❓" isn't in the list.
"✋" Stop/Hello?
"🤟" Love/ILY?
"👌" OK?
"☝" One/Up?

Maybe I should point to the wires?
Position 1-5.
I can't show positions easily with one hand.

Alternative: Just wait? No, time might matter.
Let's try gesturing "Question" or "Info".
There is no question mark.
Maybe "👆" (Up/Index finger)?
Maybe "🫵" (Point at you)? "You, talk."

Let's try pointing at myself and then making an open palm gesture "give me info"?
Symbols: 👐 (Open hands), 🤲 (Palms up).
"🤲" often means "give me" or "what?".

Plan:
Gesture `["🤲"]` to Deaf. Hope Deaf interprets this as "Give me information / What is happening?" and speaks out loud describing the bomb.

Also, I should speak to Mute. Even though Mute can't help me directly, Mute might convey info to Deaf? No, Deaf can't hear Mute. Mute can gesture to Deaf.
If I speak to Mute "Ask Deaf to describe the wires", Mute hears. Mute gestures to Deaf. Deaf sees Mute's gesture. Deaf speaks. I hear.
This is a longer chain.
Directly gesturing to Deaf is faster.

Let's combine.
Speak to Mute: "Please signal Deaf to describe the wire colors and any labels on the display."
Gesture to Deaf: `["🤲"]` (Requesting info/giving).

Actually, simpler gesture: Point at the bomb? I don't know where the bomb is relative to Deaf.
Let's stick to `["🤲"]`.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Signal Deaf to verbally describe the color of each wire (1-5) and any text on the display.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤲"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Visual report: Display shows [3]. Light is purple. Wires are numbered 1 to 5. Wire 1 is red. Wire 2 is white. Wire 3 is orange. Wire 4 is yellow. Wire 5 is green.

I have received the visual report from Deaf. I now know the colors of all five wires: 1 is red, 2 is white, 3 is orange, 4 is yellow, and 5 is green. The display shows '3' and the light is purple.

However, knowing the colors is not enough to determine which wire to cut. The manual contains the rules for defusing the bomb (e.g., "If the display is odd, cut the red wire," or specific color sequences). Mute is the only one who can read the manual.

Since I cannot see gestures, I need Mute to communicate the rule to me via speech. But Mute cannot speak. This creates a bottleneck: Mute knows the rule but cannot tell me directly. Deaf can speak to me, but Deaf does not know the rule because Deaf cannot hear Mute's gestures (if any) and Deaf cannot read the manual.

Wait, let's re-evaluate the communication channels.
- **Mute** reads the manual. Mute hears my speech. Mute sees my gestures. Mute can gesture.
- **Deaf** sees the bomb. Deaf sees my gestures. Deaf sees Mute's gestures. Deaf can speak. Deaf cannot hear.
- **Blind (Me)** hears Deaf's speech. I do not receive gestures. I cannot see.

The chain must be:
1. I ask Mute for the rule.
2. Mute gestures the rule to Deaf.
3. Deaf speaks the rule to me.

In Turn 1, I spoke to Mute asking them to signal Deaf to describe the bomb. Deaf did that. Now I need the *rule*.
I should speak to Mute, explicitly stating what I need: "What is the rule for cutting wires given Display=3 and Light=Purple?"
Mute will hear this. Mute will look at the manual. Mute will find the rule. Mute will gesture it to Deaf. Deaf will speak it to me.

So, my action is to prompt Mute to convey the specific rule to Deaf so Deaf can relay it to me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Check the manual for the rule regarding Display value 3 and Purple light. Signal the correct wire to cut to Deaf using gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: HOLD. Do not touch any wires. Mute is clarifying instructions. Wait for my next message.

I have received a verbal instruction from Deaf to HOLD and wait for further clarification from Mute. This confirms that the communication chain (Blind -> Mute -> Deaf -> Blind) is working, although it is slow. Mute has read my request and is currently formulating the correct gesture sequence to tell Deaf which wire to cut based on the manual's rules for Display=3 and Light=Purple.

Since I am explicitly told to hold and wait, any action now would be premature and potentially fatal if the rule requires a different wire or condition than what I might guess. I must remain passive until Deaf speaks again with the specific instruction.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Instruction: Cut Wire 5. It is the green wire.

Deaf has relayed the instruction from Mute: "Cut Wire 5". The visual report confirmed Wire 5 is green. I have reached the bomb and can feel the wires. Based on the manual's rules (interpreted by Mute and communicated via Deaf), cutting Wire 5 is the correct action to defuse the bomb.

```
act(op="cut", position=5)
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: New Bomb State Detected. Display shows [7]. Light is white. Remaining Wires: 1 is white, 2 is orange, 3 is yellow, 4 is red. Wire 5 is cut/gone.

The bomb has not defused; instead, it has entered a new state. The display changed from 3 to 7, the light from purple to white, and Wire 5 is gone. This implies that cutting Wire 5 was either incorrect for the final solution or triggered a secondary phase (e.g., "If wrong wire cut, reset with new parameters").

I need to know the rule for this *new* configuration: Display=7, Light=White, Wires: 1(White), 2(Orange), 3(Yellow), 4(Red).

Mute must check the manual again for these specific conditions. I will ask Mute to signal Deaf with the correct wire to cut now.

```
speak(to="mute", text="New state detected. Display is 7, Light is White. Remaining wires: 1-White, 2-Orange, 3-Yellow, 4-Red. Check manual for rule matching these conditions and signal Deaf which wire to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Instruction: Cut Wire 3. It is the yellow wire.

Deaf has relayed the instruction from Mute for the new bomb state (Display 7, Light White). The rule dictates cutting Wire 3. I can feel Wire 3 is present and distinct from the others. Following the manual's logic as interpreted by Mute, I will cut Wire 3.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[CUT] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: New Bomb State Detected. Display shows [6]. Light is yellow. Remaining Wires: 1 is orange, 2 is red, 4 is white. Wires 3 and 5 are cut.

The bomb has entered a third state. The display is now 6, the light is yellow, and the remaining wires are:
1: Orange
2: Red
4: White

I need to know which of these three wires to cut according to the manual's rules for this specific configuration (Display=6, Light=Yellow). Mute must check the manual again and signal Deaf with the correct wire number.

```
speak(to="mute", text="New state detected. Display is 6, Light is Yellow. Remaining wires: 1-Orange, 2-Red, 4-White. Check manual for rule matching these conditions and signal Deaf which wire to cut.")
```
